case_name: United States v. Service Oklahoma (OK Mobile ID App)
court: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division (administrative settlement — Title II, government entity)
docket: Administrative — DOJ investigation and settlement agreement (January 22, 2024)
industry_specific: State government digital services agency (driver's license / ID / REAL ID mobile application)
claim_type: ADA Title II — OK Mobile ID App inaccessible to blind Oklahoma residents; photo-scanning and dot-connecting enrollment tasks impossible for blind users without any verbal feedback; blocked access to unemployment benefits, REAL ID applications, and commercial transactions
settlement_disclosed: No monetary payment; corrective action required
estimated_costs: Full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for all mobile apps Service Oklahoma creates, administers or maintains; ADA coordinator requirement; ongoing public feedback mechanism; staff training

sources.name: DOJ — Justice Department Secures Agreement with Oklahoma State Agency (January 22, 2024)
DOJ — Settlement Agreement Between the United States and Service Oklahoma (January 22, 2024)
DOJ — Justice Department Finds Oklahoma Mobile App Inaccessible (November 2023)
StateScoop — Oklahoma agency, DOJ reach settlement over inaccessible mobile app

violation_source_evidence: StateScoop reporting on DOJ settlement (statescoop.com, January 22 2024): A complainant with vision disabilities 'was unable to complete necessary steps to use the mobile application, such as taking a photo of the front and back of her ID and taking a picture of herself by connecting the dots on the screen using only head and eye movements.' The OK Mobile ID app required visually-guided photo-scanning and dot-connecting enrollment tasks with no verbal feedback, making the entire onboarding flow impossible for blind users. DOJ November 2023 letter of findings confirmed app inaccessible to people with vision disabilities.
summary_one_line: DOJ forced Oklahoma's digital services agency to make its OK Mobile ID App (used for unemployment, commercial transactions, and REAL ID) WCAG 2.1 AA compliant after a blind Oklahoma resident complained the photo-scanning enrollment process was impossible without vision.
notes: DOJ letter of findings issued November 16, 2023. Settlement executed January 22, 2024. Complaint from a blind Oklahoma resident. The OK Mobile ID App allows users to create a digital version of their driver's license usable for unemployment benefits, retail purchases, and REAL ID applications. Inaccessible features: users must scan/photograph ID cards and take a selfie by connecting moving dots on screen — both tasks require sight. No verbal feedback provided. Title II case (government entity) — different from ADA Title III. Included because the app is B2B-adjacent (used for commercial transactions) and illustrates government digital services as a distinct enforcement vector. WCAG 2.1 AA required for all future apps.
